foundations.label: BA foundations
foundations.tip: Get fluent in what a BA actually does and which technique fits which situation. Start with the blog series on business process modelling and requirements prioritisation, then practise explaining the role in two sentences.

requirements.label: Requirements craft
requirements.tip: Practise turning a vague request into a problem statement, then into user stories with acceptance criteria. This is the skill interviews probe hardest.

stakeholders.label: Stakeholder skills
stakeholders.tip: Your gap is handling people, not documents. Work on running a short workshop and on facilitating disagreement with a clear prioritisation method.

delivery.label: Delivery & tools
delivery.tip: Get hands-on with how teams actually ship: sprints, backlogs, Jira, and a diagramming tool. A small practice project closes this gap fast.

career.label: Job-search readiness
career.tip: Your skills may be ahead of how you present them. Rewrite your CV and LinkedIn around BA outcomes, and prepare three STAR stories. The free interview guide is the fastest start.

questions.q: How clearly could you explain what a business analyst does, and the value they add?
Which business analysis techniques have you used on real work?
a: One or two, like a simple process map
Several: user stories, process models, stakeholder maps
I choose techniques confidently for each situation

questions.q: Have you written requirements or user stories that someone actually built from?
A stakeholder says: "We need a new dashboard." What do you do first?
a: Start listing what should go on it
Ask what data they want to see
Ask what problem the dashboard would solve
Trace it to a business objective, then test options, including not building it

questions.q: How would you feel leading a workshop with senior stakeholders?
a: Nervous, but I could do it

questions.q: Two stakeholders disagree about what should be built first. You:
a: Escalate to the manager straight away
Wait for them to sort it out
Bring them together to discuss it
Facilitate the decision with a prioritisation method and clear trade-offs

questions.q: What's your experience of Agile or Scrum teams?
a: I'm comfortable as the BA inside sprints

questions.q: Which tools are you comfortable with: Jira, a diagramming tool, Excel or Power BI, SQL?
a: Most of them, and I pick up new ones fast

questions.q: How well do your CV and LinkedIn position you for BA roles?
a: They clearly position me as a BA, with examples
They're tailored, and I'm getting responses

questions.q: An interviewer asks: "Tell me about a time you handled conflicting requirements." You:
a: Would give a vague, general answer
Have a structured story with a clear outcome

bands.title: Getting started
bands.text: You're at the beginning, which is the best place to get the route right. Most career changers lose months learning things in the wrong order. Focus on your weakest area first, and get guidance before you spend on courses or certifications.

bands.title: Building momentum
bands.text: You have real foundations. The gap now is usually specific: one or two areas that interviewers will find quickly. Closing those deliberately is what turns applications into offers.

bands.title: Interview-ready
bands.text: You're close. At this level, results come from positioning and practice: telling your experience as BA stories and rehearsing under realistic pressure. Sharpen your weakest area and start applying with confidence.
